messages:
jamie_lee: hey team, first day! quick question — for local testing and playing with streaming responses, should I be using the hosted API key or the sandbox key? I tried a quick streaming test and hit 429s after a few seconds. unsure if i'm hitting the sandbox low quota or doing something wrong with the stream client. any pointers?

alex_glenn: congrats and welcome :tada: generally: use the sandbox key for dev/local experiments. hosted keys are for staging/production and have different billing/quotas. sandbox has free credits but stricter rate buckets, especially for streaming. what endpoint are you hitting?

jamie_lee: thanks! I'm using the streaming websocket from the quickstart: wss://api.redwood.company/stream and the node sample from the docs. didn't change any default headers except Authorization.

maria_k: if you're using the quickstart websocket, sandbox streaming sits on a separate rate bucket than non-streaming calls. you can confirm your current quota usage in the Console -> Usage -> Sandbox credits. also check for 429 body: it should include a rate bucket id like "rate_bucket=sb-stream-small" which helps infra.

samir: short checklist: 1) use sandbox key for iteration 2) avoid long-running abusive loops (auto-retries) when testing streaming 3) add exponential backoff on 429s 4) if you need higher dev streaming quota, file the internal quota request form (link below) and ping #eng-infra.

samir: internal links: • quota request form: https://intranet.redwood/company-forms/compute-quota • dev guide (keys & endpoints): https://intranet.redwood/docs/dev-keys

jamie_lee: perfect — where do I find the sandbox key in the Console? I only see a Hosted API key in my profile.

alex_glenn: open Console -> API Keys -> select your org -> there should be a "Sandbox key" tab (it may be collapsed if you used up trial credits). if not visible, email dev-ops@redwood for a sandbox provisioning. alternatively, request a temporary dev key via the quota form and mention "sandbox for new hire testing".

onboarding-bot: Welcome, jamie_lee! :wave: Quick links: Getting started with keys — https://intranet.redwood/docs/dev-keys • Streaming best practices — https://intranet.redwood/docs/streaming-guide • If you run into 429s include the full response JSON and rate_bucket id when reporting.

maria_k: one more tip — for local dev you can set an env var so you don't accidentally commit keys: export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sandbox_..." and put a .env.sample without real keys in git. also use short-lived dev tokens if you're doing demos.

jamie_lee: that helps a lot, thanks everyone. i'll check Console and submit the quota form if needed. if I still hit 429s i'll paste the response and rate_bucket id here. :thumbsup:
